transcript.text: Good morning everyone. Let's get started on the production plan for the next window. We need to cover 240 Model X motor drives and 120 Model Y motor drives. I'm aware we only have 450 power modules currently released for use, with additional units sitting in quality-hold. Before I make any allocation decisions, I need input from each of you — process engineering, quality, logistics, and product compliance. Let's hear where things stand.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something important. My engineering bill-of-materials review confirms that each Model X drive requires exactly 2 power modules and each Model Y drive requires exactly 1 power module. I completed this review after the latest engineering change, but I have not yet entered the revised quantities in the planning system. This means the planning system may still be showing outdated BOM quantities. Based on these confirmed figures, producing all 240 Model X and 120 Model Y drives would require 600 power modules total — 480 for Model X plus 120 for Model Y — which exceeds the 450 currently released.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share important findings from my inspection of the quality-hold area. I found that exactly 150 of the held power modules can be recovered after a 6-hour controlled bake followed by insulation testing. I documented this result in a local inspection worksheet, but it has not yet been attached to the material record. If we proceed with the bake and testing, we could potentially have 450 released plus 150 recovered modules — 600 total — which would cover the 600 modules Ravi just confirmed we need for full production of both models.

This means Friday's shipment demand is 180 Model X plus 120 Model Y — 300 drives total — and the remaining 60 Model X drives can follow on Monday.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical compliance requirement from my destination review. Every Model Y drive must have serialized power-module traceability and a lot-specific compliance certificate before shipment. I completed the review for the export destination but have not yet added this requirement to the dispatch checklist. This means that even if we have enough power modules to produce all 120 Model Y drives, none of them can ship until the serialized traceability and lot-specific compliance certificates are in place. This is especially relevant given Jon's confirmation that all 120 Model Y drives are required on Friday.

commitments.detail: Ravi must enter the revised BOM quantities (2 power modules per Model X, 1 per Model Y) into the planning system immediately so the plan reflects accurate material requirements.

Mara must initiate the 6-hour controlled bake and insulation testing for all 150 held power modules immediately, and attach the local inspection worksheet to the material record once recovery is confirmed.

Simone must establish serialized power-module traceability and issue lot-specific compliance certificates for all 120 Model Y drives before any Model Y units ship. No Model Y drives may ship Friday until this is complete.

Jon must post the customer shipment confirmations to the shipment board immediately — 180 Model X on Friday, 60 Model X on Monday, 120 Model Y on Friday — so logistics and production scheduling are aligned.

360 of the 450 currently released power modules are allocated to Model X production and 90 to Model Y production. Once Mara confirms the 150 recovered modules pass insulation testing, 120 recovered modules are allocated to Model X and 30 to Model Y, bringing total allocation to 480 for Model X and 120 for Model Y — exactly matching the 600-module requirement.

All 120 Model Y drives may ship Friday only after Simone confirms serialized traceability and lot-specific compliance certificates are in place. If compliance is not verified by Friday, Model Y shipment will be held until verification is complete.
